changelog/CHANGELOG.html.title: Changelog | Tabular Editor
changelog/CHANGELOG.html.summary: Changelog 1.5.1 Alt+Enter (Option+Enter on macOS) while editing inserts a line break inside the cell without committing; selected text is replaced. 1.5.0 Asset path columns flag paths that can't be found with a warning icon and red text; hovering shows where Tabular Editor looked. Click N missing asset paths in the status bar to go to the next one. Dropping assets from the Project window onto a cell writes their paths in the format the column uses (Resources path or Assets/…), one per row downward. 1.4.0 Added Columns of asset paths are recognized automatically and their cells show the Project window icon. Hover for a preview card; Ctrl/Cmd+click or right-click Show in Project pings the asset. Asset path display can be turned off for all files in Preferences, or per file from the window ⋮ menu. Fixed Scrolling stuttered in files with many long cells (thousands of characters). Cells now draw only what fits; editing, copy and save still use the full value. 1.3.0 Added Ctrl+G go to a row or cell (120, C120, 120:3). Fill handle: drag to continue numbers and text ending in a number, or copy other values. Hold Alt/Option on release to swap continuing and copying. Changed The status bar shows the active cell as an address (C12). Fixed Input placeholders were not dimmed in the Android Studio theme. 1.2.0 Added English/Korean UI switch (window ⋮ menu or Preferences). Follows the OS language at first. Fixed Horizontal trackpad swipes, tilt wheels and Shift+wheel did not scroll the table sideways. 1.1.0 Added Themes (Unity / Android Studio). Frozen header rows (row number context menu Set Header Rows Up to Selection), stored in .meta and shared with your team. Find and replace: match case, regex, whole word, find in selection, vertical search, replace, replace all and preserve case. Reload files changed outside the editor right away; with unsaved edits, a notice bar asks what to do. Columns fit their content when a file opens; double-click a column border to fit again. The cell edit field grows right and down with its content. File format dialog: choose the encoding (including legacy code pages such as CP949), delimiter, quote, quote mode and line ending, then reopen or apply. Preferences > Tabular Editor: font size, mouse wheel zoom, column auto-fit and the format of new CSV files. Ascending/descending sort from the column menu (numbers and dates recognized, empty cells last). Row and column shortcuts: add (Ctrl+Alt+Arrow), jump to data edge (Ctrl+Arrow), delete (Ctrl+-), duplicate rows (Ctrl+D), move by one (Alt+Arrow) and fill the selection (Ctrl+Enter). Clicking empty space selects the nearest cell. Changed Removed the first row as header toggle and the Save and Reload buttons from the toolbar. Column titles are always A, B, C. The search button is now an icon, and the status bar shows the file format. The active cell stays at the cell where the selection started. Large files load in the background. 1.0.1 Lowered the supported version to Unity 6.0. Double-clicking .csv/.tsv files opens them on Unity 6.0 through 6.3 and later. 1.0.0 First release of Tabular Editor. File handling Added RFC 4180-compatible CSV and TSV parsing and writing, including quoted fields, embedded separators and line breaks, and escaped quotes. Preserved source encoding, BOM, line-ending style, and final-newline state. Added a TSV Scripted Importer and CSV/TSV double-click open handler. Added a confirmation before overwriting a file changed by another tool. Editing Added keyboard navigation, range selection, direct typing, F2 editing, and IME-safe text entry. Added save, dirty-state tracking, reload, and close confirmation. Added table-local Undo/Redo, clipboard operations, and cell search. Added row and column append, contextual insert/remove commands, and full row/column deletion.

manual/asset-paths.html.title: Asset paths | Tabular Editor
manual/asset-paths.html.summary: Asset paths Tabular Editor recognizes columns whose values point to assets, so you can check and enter assets right in the cells. Recognized values Format Example Resources path (no extension) Art/Sprite/Buff/spr_buff_1000 → spr_buff_1000.* under any Resources folder Project path Assets/Art/spr_buff_1000.png, Packages/… Tabular Editor looks at up to the first 50 non-empty body cells of a column (header rows excluded). If at least half of them resolve to assets, the column is treated as an asset path column. This is re-checked when a file opens, after edits, and when assets in the project change. Icons and previews Cells in an asset path column show the asset's Project window icon before the text. Hover over a cell for a moment to see a preview card. Textures and sprites show a large image and their size; other assets such as prefabs show the icon, type and path (prefabs are not loaded, because loading them can take a while). Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) a cell, or choose Show in Project from its context menu, to ping the asset in the Project window. Missing paths In an asset path column, a value that looks like a path (contains /) but resolves to no asset gets a warning icon and red text. Hovering it tells you where Tabular Editor looked. The left side of the status bar shows N missing asset paths. Each click moves to the next problem cell, wrapping around after the last. Values without / (column titles, None, - and so on) are never flagged. Drag and drop Drop assets from the Project window onto a cell to write their paths in the format the column already uses. Column Written value Uses Resources paths Art/Sprite/Shop/spr_shop_1000 Uses project paths Assets/…/spr_shop_1000.png Has no paths yet A Resources path for assets inside Resources, otherwise a project path Dropping several assets fills one cell each, downward from the target cell. The target cells are highlighted while you drag. Assets outside a Resources folder can't be dropped into a Resources path column, because Resources.Load couldn't load them. One Undo reverts the drop. Turning it off Where Scope Preferences > Tabular Editor > Asset Path Preview All files Window ⋮ menu > Asset Path Preview for This File This file only. Stored in .meta and shared with your team. Both must be on for asset paths to be shown.

manual/editing.html.title: Editing | Tabular Editor
manual/editing.html.summary: Editing Edit cells Select a cell and start typing to replace its value. F2 or a double-click edits the existing value with the caret at the end. The edit field opens two rows tall over the cell. As the text grows it widens to the right edge of the table, then wraps and grows downward. Alt+Enter (Option+Enter on macOS) inserts a line break inside the cell without committing. With a range selected, type a value and press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) to put it into every selected cell. Press Esc to cancel the edit. Every change can be undone step by step with the table's own Undo (Ctrl+Z). It never mixes with Unity's Scene Undo. Rows and columns Task How Add at the end The + buttons at the right and bottom edges Add rows above/below Ctrl+Alt+↑ / ↓, or right-click Insert Row Above / Insert Row Below Add columns left/right Ctrl+Alt+← / →, or right-click Insert Column Left / Insert Column Right Duplicate rows Ctrl+D, or right-click Duplicate Row (copies the selected rows just below) Move rows/columns by one Alt+↑ / ↓ (rows), Alt+← / → (columns) Delete Ctrl+-, right-click Delete Row / Delete Column, or select whole rows/columns and press Delete With several rows or columns selected, that many are added or deleted at once. With a cell range selected, Delete clears only the contents; Ctrl+- deletes the rows the range covers. Rows don't move across the boundary between header rows and body rows. The last remaining row or column can't be deleted. Sort Choose Sort Ascending / Sort Descending from the ▼ button on a column title or from the column title context menu. Columns of numbers sort by value (1, 2, 10), ISO dates sort as dates, and everything else sorts as case-insensitive text. Empty cells always go last, in either direction. Equal values keep their original order. Header rows are excluded. One Undo restores the previous order. Fill handle Drag the round handle at the bottom-right of the selection down, up, right or left to fill the new cells. A light blue box shows the range while you drag; dragging outside the table scrolls in that direction. Source Filled values Two or more numbers (1, 3) Continue the step (5, 7) Text ending in a number (spr_buff_1000, item_007) Count on by 1, keeping zero padding (spr_buff_1001, item_008); counts down when dragging up or left A single number, other text Copy; repeat in order when there are several Hold Alt (Option on macOS) when releasing to swap continuing and copying. Dragging a single number (1000) with Alt continues 1001, 1002…, like Ctrl-dragging in Excel. Filling upward from body rows stops at the header rows. Go to a row or cell Press Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on macOS) to open an input above the table. Input Goes to 120 Row 120 (same column) C120 Column C, row 120 120:3 Row 120, column 3 Numbers past the end go to the last row or column. Input that can't be read turns the field red. Press Enter to go; press Esc or click outside to close. Copy and paste The clipboard always holds a tab-separated rectangle, even when the file is a CSV, so you can copy to and from Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers directly.

manual/editor-interface.html.title: Editor interface | Tabular Editor
manual/editor-interface.html.summary: Editor interface From top to bottom, a Tabular Editor window has the toolbar, the find and replace bar, the external change notice bar, the table and the status bar. Toolbar and window menu The toolbar has a search icon button. Click it or press Ctrl+F to open the find and replace bar. Save with Ctrl+S or from the save prompt when closing the window (the 1.0.0 Save and Reload buttons are gone). The ⋮ menu at the top right of the window contains: Item Action Theme Choose Unity or Android Studio. Dark/light follows the Unity Editor skin. Language Choose English or 한국어. Applies to the whole window immediately. Asset Path Preview for This File Turn asset path display on or off for this file only. Preferences... Open Preferences > Tabular Editor. Table Column titles are always A, B, C… Click a title to select the column; drag across titles to select several. Hover a column title and click the ▼ button to open the sort menu. Drag the right edge of a column title to resize; double-click it to fit the content. Columns with values also fit their content when a file opens. Click a row number to select the row; drag to select several. Set header rows from the row number context menu. The selection has a blue outline; the round dot at its bottom-right is the fill handle. The + buttons at the right and bottom edges add a column and a row at the end. Clicking the empty space right of the last column or below the last row selects the nearest cell. The mouse wheel scrolls vertically; Shift+wheel and horizontal trackpad swipes scroll horizontally. Ctrl+wheel (Cmd+wheel on macOS) changes the font size. Find and replace bar See Find and replace. External change notice bar When another program changes the open file, Tabular Editor reloads it right away. Only when you have unsaved edits does a notice bar appear above the table: choose Reload (discard your edits and read the file) or Ignore (keep your edits; you are asked again whether to overwrite when you save). Status bar Position Shows Left Table size (120 rows × 8 columns) Active cell address and details (C12 (4 chars), 54 cells for a range, 3 rows · Delete to remove for whole rows or columns) 3 missing asset paths when an asset path column has problems — click to go to the next one Right Unsaved Encoding, line ending (LF/CRLF), delimiter and quoting rule — click to open the file format dialog The active cell address (C12) can be typed straight into Ctrl+G go to.

manual/file-format.html.title: File format | Tabular Editor
manual/file-format.html.summary: File format Click the encoding, line ending or delimiter on the right of the status bar to open the CSV File Format dialog (TSV File Format for TSV files). Item Choices Encoding UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, Korean (CP949, EUC-KR), Japanese (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP), Chinese (GBK, GB18030, Big5), Windows 1252 and more Delimiter Comma, Tab, Semicolon, Colon, Pipe, Space, Other (type one character) Quote None, ", ', Other (type one character) Quote Mode Always, Minimal (only cells with the delimiter, a quote or a line break), Never Line Ending LF, CRLF Final Newline Whether the file ends with a line break Reopen and Apply Reopen: reads the file from disk again in the chosen format. Unsaved edits are discarded. For example, a CP949 file that shows garbled text opens correctly after choosing Korean (CP949) and reopening. Apply: keeps the cell values and changes only the format used when saving. It takes effect in the file when you save and can be undone. What is stored in .meta Anything that can't be detected from a BOM or the extension (a legacy encoding, or a non-default delimiter, quote or quote mode) is written to the file's .meta (userData). The file opens the same way next time and for teammates who get it through version control. When everything is default, the .meta is left unchanged. Note If another tool already uses the file's userData, Tabular Editor doesn't overwrite it and logs a warning in the Console.

manual/find-and-replace.html.title: Find and replace | Tabular Editor
manual/find-and-replace.html.summary: Find and replace Open the find and replace bar with the toolbar's search icon or Ctrl+F. Matching cells are highlighted in the table. Find The toggles on the right side of the input set how to search. Toggle Effect Match case Distinguishes Cat from cat. Use regular expression Treats the search text as a regular expression. An invalid pattern shows Invalid regex. Match whole word Matches whole words only. The buttons next to the input: Next / Previous match: same as Enter / Shift+Enter or F3 / Shift+F3. The position is shown as 3/12. Find in selection: searches only the current selection. Search vertically: scans column by column, top to bottom. When off, it scans row by row, left to right. Close: same as Esc. Replace Click the expand button on the left (Toggle replace) to show the replace row. Replace (Enter): replaces the selected match and moves to the next one. When no match is selected yet, the first press only moves to the first match. Replace all (Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter on macOS): replaces every match at once and shows how many cells changed. One Undo reverts it. Preserve case (AB): matches the letter case of the replaced text to the original. With regular expressions on, the replacement can use group references such as $1.

manual/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | Tabular Editor
manual/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Open a table Double-click a .csv or .tsv asset in the Project window. To open an empty window without a file, use Window > NKStudio > Tabular Editor. Tabular Editor opens one window per asset. Double-clicking the same file again focuses the existing window. Large files are read in the background, so the editor stays responsive while loading. Create a new CSV file Choose Create > Scripting > CSV File in the Project window to create an empty table and name it right away. The size (5×5 by default) and format, such as encoding and delimiter, come from New CSV File in Preferences. Edit and save Click a cell to make it active. Type to replace the value, or press F2 or double-click to edit the existing value. Press Enter to commit and move down, or Tab to commit and move right. To start a new line inside the cell, press Alt+Enter (Option+Enter on macOS). Save with Ctrl+S on Windows/Linux or Cmd+S on macOS. With unsaved changes, the window tab shows * and the status bar shows Unsaved. Closing the window without saving asks whether to save. Freeze header rows Right-click a row number on the far left of the table to open the header row menu. Right-click the row number of the last row you want to freeze. To freeze only the top row, right-click 1. Choose Set Header Rows Up to Selection. Every row from row 1 to the one you clicked becomes a header row. Those rows stay at the top in bold while you scroll vertically. Header rows can still be selected and edited; they are only excluded from sorting. To undo it, choose Clear Header Rows from the row number context menu. The header row count is stored in the file's .meta and shared with your team through version control. Next steps See Editor interface for what each area does. Learn rows and columns, sorting and the fill handle in Editing. See Keyboard shortcuts for the full list.

manual/index.html.title: Tabular Editor | Tabular Editor
manual/index.html.summary: Tabular Editor Tabular Editor is a UI Toolkit editor for CSV and TSV files inside Unity. Double-click a supported asset to open it as a table, edit cells with familiar spreadsheet controls, and save back to the original text file. Features Double-click .csv and .tsv assets to open and edit them as a table. Range selection, row/column editing, sorting and a fill handle (1001, 1002…). Frozen header rows, find and replace with regex, and Ctrl+G go-to. Icons and previews for asset-path columns, with drag-and-drop from the Project window. Saving preserves the original encoding (including CP949), line endings and quoting. Editor-only, with no runtime API and no external packages. Check the requirements, then follow Installation and Getting started. Changes since 1.0.0 are listed in the changelog.

manual/installation.html.title: Installation | Tabular Editor
manual/installation.html.summary: Installation Tabular Editor installs as a single Git package with no additional dependencies. Install with the Unity Package Manager In Unity, open Window > Package Manager. Click + and choose Install package from git URL.... Enter the following URL and click Install. https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.unitytable.git Add to the manifest directly You can also add the package to the dependencies object in Packages/manifest.json. { "dependencies": { "com.nkstudio.unitytable": "https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.unitytable.git" } } Keep the other dependencies already in your manifest. Verify the installation After Unity finishes importing and compiling, check that: Tabular Editor appears in the Package Manager. The Console shows no compile errors from the package. Double-clicking a .csv or .tsv asset opens it in Tabular Editor. No additional plugins or dependencies are required.

manual/preferences.html.title: Preferences | Tabular Editor
manual/preferences.html.summary: Preferences Open Edit > Preferences > Tabular Editor (Unity > Settings > Tabular Editor on macOS) or choose Preferences... from the window's ⋮ menu. Values are stored per user (EditorPrefs), so teammates on the same project can set them differently. Reset to Defaults restores the original values. Display Item Description Language Language of the window, menus and this page (English / 한국어). Follows the OS language at first. Theme Unity / Android Studio. Dark/light follows the Unity Editor skin. Font Size 8–32. Row height, row number width and column widths scale with it. Mouse Wheel Zoom When on, Ctrl+wheel (Cmd+wheel on macOS) changes the font size. Asset Path Preview Turns asset path display on or off for all files. Column Auto-Fit Item Description On File Open Fits columns that have values to their content. On Cell Edit Widens a column when an edited value no longer fits. Never shrinks a column you widened yourself. Rows to Scan Number of rows, from the top, examined to decide a width (3000 by default). Header rows are always examined. Max Width (% of Window) Maximum width a column can grow to automatically (70% by default). New CSV File Sets the rows and columns (5×5 by default) and the encoding, delimiter, quote, quote mode, line ending and final newline of files created with Create > Scripting > CSV File. A format other than the default (UTF-8, comma, double quote, minimal) is recorded in the .meta so the file is read the same way when opened.

manual/requirements.html.title: Requirements | Tabular Editor
manual/requirements.html.summary: Requirements Supported Unity versions Tabular Editor 1.5.1 requires Unity 6000.0 or later. UI Toolkit ships with the Unity Editor, so no separate UI package is required. Supported files Extension Default delimiter Notes .csv Comma Supports quoted fields with commas, quotes and line breaks inside. .tsv Tab Imported by the package's Scripted Importer and edited in the same editor. The delimiter and quote character can be changed per file in the file format dialog (semicolon, pipe and so on). Files must be inside the Unity project so they appear as assets in the Project window. You can open writable files under Assets and under installed or embedded Packages. Encoding support UTF-8 with or without BOM, UTF-16 Little Endian and UTF-16 Big Endian are detected from the file. Without a recognizable BOM, the file is read as UTF-8 without BOM. For legacy code pages such as CP949, EUC-KR, Shift_JIS or GBK, choose the encoding in the file format dialog and reopen the file. The choice is stored in the .meta so the file opens with that encoding next time.

manual/shortcuts.html.title: Keyboard shortcuts | Tabular Editor
manual/shortcuts.html.summary: Keyboard shortcuts Use Cmd instead of Ctrl and Option instead of Alt on macOS. Moving and selecting Shortcut Action Arrow keys Move the active cell. Shift+Arrow keys Extend the selection. Ctrl+Arrow keys Jump to the end of the filled run, the next value, or the table edge (Excel style). Add Shift to extend the selection. Tab / Shift+Tab Move right/left and wrap at row boundaries. Enter / Shift+Enter Move down/up; commit first when editing. Home / End Move to the first/last column in the row. Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End Move to the first/last cell in the table. Page Up / Page Down Move by approximately one visible page. Ctrl+G Go to a row or cell (120, C120). Ctrl+A Select all. Editing Shortcut Action F2 or double-click Edit the existing cell value. Typing Replace the active cell and begin editing. Alt+Enter (while editing) Insert a line break inside the cell. Ctrl+Enter (while editing) Put the typed value into every selected cell. Esc Cancel editing. Delete / Backspace Clear cells, or delete whole rows/columns when they are selected. Rows and columns Shortcut Action Ctrl+Alt+↓ / ↑ Add rows below/above (as many as selected). Ctrl+Alt+→ / ← Add columns right/left (as many as selected). Ctrl+- Delete the selected rows, or columns when columns are selected. Ctrl+D Duplicate the selected rows just below. Alt+↑ / ↓ Move the selected rows up/down by one. Alt+← / → Move the selected columns left/right by one. File and clipboard Shortcut Action Ctrl+S Save. Ctrl+Z Undo. Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y Redo. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V Copy / cut / paste. Ctrl+F Open find and replace. F3 / Shift+F3 Next / previous search match. Mouse Action Effect Wheel / Shift+wheel / horizontal trackpad swipe Scroll vertically / horizontally. Ctrl+wheel Change the font size. Drag the fill handle Continue values; hold Alt on release to swap continuing and copying. Ctrl+click an asset cell Ping the asset in the Project window. During an edit started with F2 or a double-click, arrow keys move the caret. During an edit started by typing, arrow keys commit the value and move to the adjacent cell.
